Sunday, November 15

Game recap

SEA1CAR5Final: SEA 1, CAR 5

Carolina packed up Helsinki with a 5-1 win and a two-game sweep of Seattle, which is a long way to fly to get your homework graded twice. The power play did the damage: Jackson Blake opened it up with the man advantage, and Andrei Svechnikov scored twice more on it, with Nikolaj Ehlers setting up three goals. Mark Jankowski chipped in two of his own, and Jordan Staal played 13:55 in his first game back after missing 14. Joey Daccord was pulled after letting in four on 14 shots, Philipp Grubauer stopped 22 of 23 the rest of the way, and Matty Beniers got Seattle's only goal. Pyotr Kochetkov needed just 12 saves, and Jagger Firkus made his NHL debut in a game that was over by the second intermission. The Kraken put 13 shots on net across a whole hockey game, about what they'd manage from the Climate Pledge parking lot.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

WPG5CHI4SOFinal: WPG 5, CHI 4 SO

Chicago led 4-0 midway through the second period and still lost, which takes a special kind of commitment. Tyler Bertuzzi, Anton Frondell and Connor Bedard (power play) chased Stuart Skinner after one period (three goals on eight shots), Frank Nazar made it 4-0 on another power play, and then the Blackhawks went back to being the Blackhawks. Mark Scheifele started the comeback at 16:05 of the second, Kyle Connor and Cole Perfetti (power play) followed, and Gabriel Vilardi tied it with 1:13 left and the goalie pulled. Scheifele finished with a goal and three assists, set the Jets' franchise points record, and scored in the shootout too; Connor added the winner there, with Patrick Kane the only Hawk to beat Nico Daws, who stopped 12 of 13 in relief. Spencer Knight made 27 saves. In Chicago a four-goal lead isn't a cushion, it's a loan, and the Jets called it in.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MIN6BOS2Final: MIN 6, BOS 2

Minnesota walked into TD Garden and treated it like a rental: 6-2, an eighth straight road win and an 11-game point streak. Ryan Hartman scored twice, Danila Yurov scored twice (the second into an empty net), and Quinn Hughes and Blake Coleman also scored, Coleman adding two assists. Kirill Kaprizov set up two, and Brock Faber got an assist in his season debut, the kind of welcome-back gift most guys only get in their dreams. Fraser Minten on the power play and David Pastrnak cut it to 4-2, then Yurov answered 90 seconds later. Jesper Wallstedt stopped 30 of 32; Jeremy Swayman saw 24 shots and let five through. Marcus Foligno and Tanner Jeannot fought in the second, which was Boston's best stretch of the night. The Bruins wanted a statement game and got one: it just had the Wild's name on it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

EDM1TOR0Final: EDM 1, TOR 0

Devon Levi got his first NHL shutout, and Toronto made it easy for him: 19 shots, all saved, in a 1-0 Oilers win. The only goal came at 15:34 of the second, Evan Bouchard finishing off Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl, which stretches McDavid's point streak to 21 games. Anthony Stolarz was terrific at the other end, 22 saves on 23, and got exactly the run support he's come to expect. John Tavares thought he'd tied it late, but the goal was waved off, the perfect ending to a homestand the Leafs finished 0-6, now six straight losses. Colton Dach and Brandon Duhaime fought in the first, the closest Toronto came to winning anything all night. Leafs fans paid full price to watch a team that can't score in its own building, which at least makes it a very Toronto tradition.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

COL4MTL1Final: COL 4, MTL 1

Colorado played its first game without Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar and won 4-1 in Montreal anyway, which is either great depth or a very bad sign for the Canadiens. It ended Montreal's 12-game point streak. Fedor Svechkov opened the scoring, Brock Nelson made it 2-0 with an extra attacker on late in the first, and after Nick Suzuki got one back in the second, Artturi Lehkonen scored his 15th on the power play and Nicolas Roy hit the empty net. Mackenzie Blackwood stopped 25 of 26, Jakub Dobes 23 of 26. Alex Gagne made his NHL debut beside Brent Burns, who played his 1,600th game, so the Avs' blue line went from first night to forever on one pair. Montreal spent two weeks looking like a contender and then lost to the Avalanche's understudies.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DET2TBL0Final: DET 2, TBL 0

Daniil Tarasov stopped all 31 shots and Detroit won 2-0 in Tampa, ending its five-game skid and the Lightning's home streak in one go. Lucas Raymond scored the only goal that mattered, at 13:12 of the second from William Wallinder, and set up Michael Brandsegg-Nygård's empty-netter with 43 seconds left. Andrei Vasilevskiy was nearly as good, 20 saves on 21, and lost anyway, because Tampa played without Anthony Cirelli and Erik Cernak and couldn't solve a goalie who got the start after John Gibson gave up five in Florida. The Red Wings needed a win like they need Dylan Larkin to pick up the phone, and they got one. Tampa had 31 shots and zero goals, the hockey version of working a double and going home broke.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

OTT4PIT1Final: OTT 4, PIT 1

Linus Ullmark picked up his 200th NHL win in Pittsburgh, and the Penguins barely made him work for it: 16 saves on 17 in a 4-1 Senators win that runs Ottawa's point streak to five. Tommy Novak gave Pittsburgh a lead with eight seconds left in the first, and that was the last fun the home crowd had. Michael Amadio tied it with an unassisted goal and then set up Claude Giroux, Tim Stützle added his 11th in the third, and Thomas Chabot finished it into the empty net. Sergei Murashov kept it close with 30 saves on 33. Ottawa outshot Pittsburgh 34-17, which is the kind of gap you usually see between the NHL and the AHL. The Penguins are 7-11-2 and Kyle Dubas is reportedly warming up the sell button, and nights like this are why.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NJD7WSH4Final: NJD 7, WSH 4

Washington threw 47 shots at Connor Hellebuyck, scored four, and still lost 7-4, because the Devils got their own goalie and the Capitals got whatever Charlie Lindgren was doing (26 saves on 32). Hellebuyck made 43 saves and is 7-0-0 as a Devil, a franchise record. The Caps led three times in the first, 1-0, 2-1 and 3-2, on goals from Pierre-Luc Dubois, Ryan Leonard and Anthony Beauvillier, and Cole Hutson set up three. Then New Jersey took over: Jesper Boqvist tied it, Timo Meier scored on the power play, and Nico Hischier's shorthanded goal 56 seconds into the third was the winner. Evan Rodrigues scored twice, Lenni Hameenaho had a goal and two assists, and Luke Hughes three assists, while Anton Silaev made his NHL debut. The Capitals outshot the Devils by 15 and lost by three, which is advanced stats' way of saying 'nice try.'

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

PHI4CBJ3Final: PHI 4, CBJ 3

Columbus scored twice in the first 4:19 on home ice, and the Flyers, a team that scores like it's paying per goal, answered with four. Dmitri Voronkov's first of the season and Matthew Knies put the Blue Jackets up 2-0. Trevor Zegras, an unassisted Matvei Michkov and a Denver Barkey power-play goal made it 3-2 early in the second; Adam Fantilli tied it, and Barkey won it at 11:54 of the third off Noel Acciari's setup. Joseph Woll stopped 28 of 31, Jet Greaves 17 of 21, and Owen Tippett and Dante Fabbro fought in the second. Columbus played without Sean Monahan and is 7-11-0. Blowing a two-goal lead to the Flyers' offense is like getting outrun by a Zamboni.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

FLA4STL1Final: FLA 4, STL 1

St. Louis honored Keith Tkachuk before the game, and his sons said thanks by beating the Blues: Brady Tkachuk scored the power-play opener, with Matthew Tkachuk on the assist, in a 4-1 Florida win. Dmitry Kulikov scored his first of the season a minute later, Anton Lundell made it 3-0 in the second, and Sam Reinhart's unassisted goal in the third, his 12th, came on a night he reached 700 career points. Jacob Markstrom stopped 23 of 24 and lost the shutout to Dylan Holloway's power-play goal with 2:06 left. Joel Hofer made 24 saves on 28 in his fourth straight start. Radko Gudas played his 900th game. It was a lovely ceremony for the Tkachuk family, and then the family took two points home to Florida, the most Blues thing imaginable.

Game recap

BUF0DAL2Final: BUF 0, DAL 2

Jamie Benn got his 1,000th career point, every one of them in a Dallas sweater, and it was the goal that beat Buffalo 2-0. Benn scored at 16:23 of the second off Justin Hryckowian and Nils Lundkvist, and Wyatt Johnston added a power-play goal with 42 seconds left. Jake Oettinger needed only 22 saves for his fourth shutout, which says a lot about the Sabres' night. Alex Lyon was good in his second straight start, 28 saves on 30, and got nothing for it. Dallas is 11-6-2; Buffalo is 8-8-4 and has now been shut out by a goalie who could have played the third period in a recliner. A thousand points for Benn, zero for the Sabres: that's been the Buffalo experience for about 15 years.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SJS6UTA5SOFinal: SJS 6, UTA 5 SO

Ten goals in 65 minutes, two fights and a shootout, and San Jose came out of Utah with a 6-5 win and Utah with a fifth straight loss. Zac Jones scored twice as Utah led 3-1 and 4-3, but the Sharks kept coming: Tyler Toffoli and Adam Gaudette on the power play, Zack Ostapchuk, then Eric Pohlkamp's first NHL goal to tie it at 4 in the third. Dmitry Orlov put the Sharks ahead with 5:43 left and finished with four points; Barrett Hayton tied it again on the power play two minutes later. In the shootout Vincent Trocheck and Macklin Celebrini traded goals before Mason Marchment won it in the fifth round. Karel Vejmelka gave up five on 21 shots (Andre Tourigny said afterward 'Vej has to be better'), and Yaroslav Askarov made 27 saves. Andrew Peeke fought Ty Dellandrea and then Gaudette. Utah's defense went the full 65 minutes without showing up, a real commitment to the bit.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYI6ANA2Final: NYI 6, ANA 2

Simon Holmstrom picked a good night for his first career hat trick: the Islanders beat Anaheim 6-2, and Mathew Barzal got an assist on Ben Hutton's goal 1:55 into his season debut. Bo Horvat scored on the power play, Holmstrom scored twice in 5:27 of the second, Mitchell Chaffee made it 5-1, and Holmstrom finished the job early in the third. Matthew Schaefer had three assists, because apparently the 19-year-old is also the Isles' playmaker now. Semyon Varlamov stopped 26 of 28; Lukas Dostal stayed in for all 60 minutes and six goals on 25 shots, which is the kind of loyalty usually reserved for a bad contract. Nikita Nesterenko and Cutter Gauthier (his 17th) scored for the Ducks. The Ducks were down 5-1 before the game was half over, then left their goalie out there to absorb a sixth: that's not goaltending support, that's a dare.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CGY3LAK2Final: CGY 3, LAK 2

Calgary opened its road trip with a 3-2 win in Los Angeles, and the Kings helped. Morgan Frost scored early in the second off a Cody Ceci turnover, and Ceci watched the third period from the bench. Joel Armia tied it at 6:21 of the third, Matvei Gridin answered five minutes later for the winner, and Yegor Sharangovich hit the empty net with 1:14 left. Mats Zuccarello's first of the season with the goalie pulled made it close 18 seconds later. Dustin Wolf stopped 29 of 31; Anton Forsberg 21 of 23. The Kings are 5-11-2, level with Chicago at 12 points and ahead of only Vancouver, a Hollywood ending nobody in LA wanted to see.

Saturday, November 14

Game recap

NYR5VAN1Final: NYR 5, VAN 1

Vancouver hung around for a period, which at this point counts as a moral victory. Elias Pettersson opened the scoring at 12:13 of the first, Gabe Perreault answered before intermission, and then the second period happened: four Rangers goals in 7:49. Oliver Bjorkstrand scored on the power play, Glenn Gawdin got his first NHL goal unassisted, Alexis Lafrenière buried his 10th, and Gawdin added his second just 56 seconds later. A guy who played 7:59 had two goals; the entire Canucks lineup had one. J.T. Miller set up two against his old team, Dylan Garand stopped 27 of 28, and Leevi Meriläinen made 26 saves on 31. New York is 12-8-1. Vancouver is 3-17-1 with seven straight losses, and the only thing the Canucks are building right now is a lottery ticket.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NSH3VGK2SOFinal: NSH 3, VGK 2 SO

Vegas threw 42 shots at Juuse Saros and got two past him, so naturally this one needed a shootout. Ryan O'Reilly scored at 7:56 of the first, Victor Olofsson tied it, and Rasmus Andersson put Vegas ahead in the second. O'Reilly tied it again at 9:44 of the third, his second of the night and ninth of the season, and overtime settled nothing. In the shootout Trevor Connelly scored for Vegas, Filip Forsberg answered, Jack Eichel was stopped and Roman Josi ended it, after playing 31:40 and apparently still having legs. Saros made 40 saves; Adin Hill made 30 on 32. Nashville has won seven straight and is 11-4-5. Vegas outshot its guests by 10 and went home with one point, which in that town is called breaking even and still feels like losing.

nhl.com ↗
VAN
News

Gawdin scores his first two NHL goals as the Rangers beat the Canucks 5-1, Vancouver's seventh straight loss

Elias Pettersson opened the scoring with his first 5-on-5 goal since Jan. 13, but New York scored four in the second and Dylan Garand made 27 saves. Brock Boeser's assist was his 500th career point. The Canucks are 3-17-1 and 1-16-1 in their last 18 games.

nhl.com ↗
STL
News

Blues honor Keith Tkachuk before the Florida game, two days before his Hall of Fame induction

St. Louis holds a pregame ceremony for Tkachuk, a former Blue who now advises the front office, ahead of his Hockey Hall of Fame induction Monday. His sons Matthew and Brady take part in the ceremonial puck drop.

floridahockeynow.com ↗

Correction · Nov 14: The ceremony honored Tkachuk's Hall of Fame induction earlier in the week; it came after the induction, not before it. nhl.com ↗

Confirmed · Nov 14: NHL.com's recap confirms the Blues honored Tkachuk before the game for his Hockey Hall of Fame induction. nhl.com ↗

FLA
News

Radko Gudas set for his 900th NHL game in St. Louis

Paul Maurice marked the milestone: 'That's 900 hard games,' guessing it adds up to about 2,500 hits and 1,200 blocked shots.

nhl.com ↗
CAR
News

Carolina beats Seattle 5-1 to sweep the Helsinki series; Staal plays 13:55 in his return and Daccord is pulled

Andrei Svechnikov and Mark Jankowski scored twice each, Nikolaj Ehlers had three assists and Pyotr Kochetkov made 12 saves on Seattle's 13 shots. Jordan Staal played 13:55 after missing 14 games with a torn calf; Joey Daccord was pulled after four goals on 14 shots, and Jagger Firkus played 11:38 in his NHL debut as the Kraken lost a third straight.

nhl.com ↗
WPG
News

Jets come back from 4-0 down to beat Chicago 5-4 in a shootout as Scheifele sets the franchise points record

Scheifele had a goal and three assists for 933 career points, passing Dale Hawerchuk's 929, and Vilardi tied it with 1:13 left. Nico Daws replaced Stuart Skinner after Skinner allowed three goals on eight shots in the first period. Kane's assist moved him past Hawerchuk into 23rd on the NHL's career points list, and Winnipeg has now won six straight.

nhl.com ↗
TOR
News

Leafs lose a sixth straight, 1-0 to Edmonton, and go 0-6 on the homestand; Tavares' late tying goal waved off

Toronto (8-12-2) lost every game of the homestand in regulation and was outscored 23-9. Devon Levi made 19 saves for his first NHL shutout, Evan Bouchard scored the only goal, and review found Tavares tipped the third-period puck with a high stick. McDavid's season-opening point streak is now 21 games.

nhl.com ↗
MTL
News

Colorado ends Montreal's 12-game point streak with a 4-1 win, its first game without MacKinnon and Makar

The Canadiens had gone 9-0-3 since an Oct. 14 loss in Washington. Nick Suzuki scored Montreal's only goal in its first game without Chris Kreider, while Artturi Lehkonen had a goal and an assist and Mackenzie Blackwood made 25 saves.

nhl.com ↗
DAL
News

Jamie Benn reaches 1,000 career points, all with Dallas, as Oettinger's 22-save shutout beats Buffalo 2-0

Benn's second-period goal makes him the second player in franchise history to 1,000 points, behind Mike Modano. Jake Oettinger got his fourth shutout of the season two days after he was pulled in the 8-3 loss to Winnipeg.

sports.yahoo.com ↗
FLA
News

Brady Tkachuk scores on the power play as Florida wins 4-1 in St. Louis; Reinhart reaches 700 career points

Kulikov, with his first of the season, and Lundell also scored, and Reinhart's assist on Tkachuk's goal was his 700th NHL point. Markstrom made 23 saves, losing the shutout to Dylan Holloway's power-play goal late in the third. Florida plays in Dallas on Sunday.

nhl.com ↗
COL
News

Avalanche win 4-1 in Montreal without MacKinnon and Makar, ending the Canadiens' 12-game point streak

Mackenzie Blackwood made 25 saves and Artturi Lehkonen scored on the power play, his third straight game with a goal, and added an assist. Colorado (12-6-3) has points in five straight; Montreal had gone 9-0-3.

nhl.com ↗
MIN
News

Wild beat Boston 6-2 for an eighth straight road win and an 11-game point streak; Faber has an assist in his debut

Ryan Hartman and Danila Yurov each scored twice and Jesper Wallstedt made 30 saves; Swayman made 19 for Boston. Brock Faber played 24:29 with an assist and a plus-4 in his first game since fracturing his skull in the preseason.

nhl.com ↗
PHI
News

Longtime Flyers team physician Dr. Gary Dorshimer dies

The Flyers announced the death of Dorshimer, who cared for the team over several decades. Chairman and CEO Dan Hilferty said the club was deeply saddened.

nhl.com ↗
OTT
News

Ullmark earns his 200th NHL win as Ottawa beats Pittsburgh 4-1 and extends its point streak to five

Amadio had a goal and an assist, and Giroux, Stutzle and Chabot (empty net) also scored. Ullmark made 16 saves and is the fourth Sweden-born goalie to 200 wins, the fastest of them at 350 games. Ottawa is 13-6-2.

Goalie prospect Trey Augustine posts his first pro shutout as AHL Grand Rapids beats Iowa 3-0

Augustine stopped 31 shots in Friday's win over the Iowa Wild. The Griffins are near the top of the AHL standings.

Crotty, claimed off waivers from Minnesota on Tuesday, played 12:18 in his first game for Vancouver. Tom Willander had three shots in 17:04 after missing four games with a lower-body injury, and Filip Chytil played 17:14 in his return from a shoulder injury.

Carolina HurricanesCAR16-3-2 · 34 pts37 shots
1st2nd3rdTSEA0101CAR2215

Puckline's Report

Carolina packed up Helsinki with a 5-1 win and a two-game sweep of Seattle, which is a long way to fly to get your homework graded twice. The power play did the damage: Jackson Blake opened it up with the man advantage, and Andrei Svechnikov scored twice more on it, with Nikolaj Ehlers setting up three goals. Mark Jankowski chipped in two of his own, and Jordan Staal played 13:55 in his first game back after missing 14. Joey Daccord was pulled after letting in four on 14 shots, Philipp Grubauer stopped 22 of 23 the rest of the way, and Matty Beniers got Seattle's only goal. Pyotr Kochetkov needed just 12 saves, and Jagger Firkus made his NHL debut in a game that was over by the second intermission. The Kraken put 13 shots on net across a whole hockey game, about what they'd manage from the Climate Pledge parking lot.

By Puckline Prince

Chicago BlackhawksCHI5-13-2 · 12 pts21 shots
1st2nd3rdOTSOTWPG022015CHI310004

Puckline's Report

Chicago led 4-0 midway through the second period and still lost, which takes a special kind of commitment. Tyler Bertuzzi, Anton Frondell and Connor Bedard (power play) chased Stuart Skinner after one period (three goals on eight shots), Frank Nazar made it 4-0 on another power play, and then the Blackhawks went back to being the Blackhawks. Mark Scheifele started the comeback at 16:05 of the second, Kyle Connor and Cole Perfetti (power play) followed, and Gabriel Vilardi tied it with 1:13 left and the goalie pulled. Scheifele finished with a goal and three assists, set the Jets' franchise points record, and scored in the shootout too; Connor added the winner there, with Patrick Kane the only Hawk to beat Nico Daws, who stopped 12 of 13 in relief. Spencer Knight made 27 saves. In Chicago a four-goal lead isn't a cushion, it's a loan, and the Jets called it in.

Puckline's Report

Minnesota walked into TD Garden and treated it like a rental: 6-2, an eighth straight road win and an 11-game point streak. Ryan Hartman scored twice, Danila Yurov scored twice (the second into an empty net), and Quinn Hughes and Blake Coleman also scored, Coleman adding two assists. Kirill Kaprizov set up two, and Brock Faber got an assist in his season debut, the kind of welcome-back gift most guys only get in their dreams. Fraser Minten on the power play and David Pastrnak cut it to 4-2, then Yurov answered 90 seconds later. Jesper Wallstedt stopped 30 of 32; Jeremy Swayman saw 24 shots and let five through. Marcus Foligno and Tanner Jeannot fought in the second, which was Boston's best stretch of the night. The Bruins wanted a statement game and got one: it just had the Wild's name on it.

Puckline's Report

Devon Levi got his first NHL shutout, and Toronto made it easy for him: 19 shots, all saved, in a 1-0 Oilers win. The only goal came at 15:34 of the second, Evan Bouchard finishing off Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl, which stretches McDavid's point streak to 21 games. Anthony Stolarz was terrific at the other end, 22 saves on 23, and got exactly the run support he's come to expect. John Tavares thought he'd tied it late, but the goal was waved off, the perfect ending to a homestand the Leafs finished 0-6, now six straight losses. Colton Dach and Brandon Duhaime fought in the first, the closest Toronto came to winning anything all night. Leafs fans paid full price to watch a team that can't score in its own building, which at least makes it a very Toronto tradition.

Puckline's Report

Colorado played its first game without Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar and won 4-1 in Montreal anyway, which is either great depth or a very bad sign for the Canadiens. It ended Montreal's 12-game point streak. Fedor Svechkov opened the scoring, Brock Nelson made it 2-0 with an extra attacker on late in the first, and after Nick Suzuki got one back in the second, Artturi Lehkonen scored his 15th on the power play and Nicolas Roy hit the empty net. Mackenzie Blackwood stopped 25 of 26, Jakub Dobes 23 of 26. Alex Gagne made his NHL debut beside Brent Burns, who played his 1,600th game, so the Avs' blue line went from first night to forever on one pair. Montreal spent two weeks looking like a contender and then lost to the Avalanche's understudies.

Puckline's Report

Daniil Tarasov stopped all 31 shots and Detroit won 2-0 in Tampa, ending its five-game skid and the Lightning's home streak in one go. Lucas Raymond scored the only goal that mattered, at 13:12 of the second from William Wallinder, and set up Michael Brandsegg-Nygård's empty-netter with 43 seconds left. Andrei Vasilevskiy was nearly as good, 20 saves on 21, and lost anyway, because Tampa played without Anthony Cirelli and Erik Cernak and couldn't solve a goalie who got the start after John Gibson gave up five in Florida. The Red Wings needed a win like they need Dylan Larkin to pick up the phone, and they got one. Tampa had 31 shots and zero goals, the hockey version of working a double and going home broke.

Puckline's Report

Linus Ullmark picked up his 200th NHL win in Pittsburgh, and the Penguins barely made him work for it: 16 saves on 17 in a 4-1 Senators win that runs Ottawa's point streak to five. Tommy Novak gave Pittsburgh a lead with eight seconds left in the first, and that was the last fun the home crowd had. Michael Amadio tied it with an unassisted goal and then set up Claude Giroux, Tim Stützle added his 11th in the third, and Thomas Chabot finished it into the empty net. Sergei Murashov kept it close with 30 saves on 33. Ottawa outshot Pittsburgh 34-17, which is the kind of gap you usually see between the NHL and the AHL. The Penguins are 7-11-2 and Kyle Dubas is reportedly warming up the sell button, and nights like this are why.

Puckline's Report

Washington threw 47 shots at Connor Hellebuyck, scored four, and still lost 7-4, because the Devils got their own goalie and the Capitals got whatever Charlie Lindgren was doing (26 saves on 32). Hellebuyck made 43 saves and is 7-0-0 as a Devil, a franchise record. The Caps led three times in the first, 1-0, 2-1 and 3-2, on goals from Pierre-Luc Dubois, Ryan Leonard and Anthony Beauvillier, and Cole Hutson set up three. Then New Jersey took over: Jesper Boqvist tied it, Timo Meier scored on the power play, and Nico Hischier's shorthanded goal 56 seconds into the third was the winner. Evan Rodrigues scored twice, Lenni Hameenaho had a goal and two assists, and Luke Hughes three assists, while Anton Silaev made his NHL debut. The Capitals outshot the Devils by 15 and lost by three, which is advanced stats' way of saying 'nice try.'

Puckline's Report

Columbus scored twice in the first 4:19 on home ice, and the Flyers, a team that scores like it's paying per goal, answered with four. Dmitri Voronkov's first of the season and Matthew Knies put the Blue Jackets up 2-0. Trevor Zegras, an unassisted Matvei Michkov and a Denver Barkey power-play goal made it 3-2 early in the second; Adam Fantilli tied it, and Barkey won it at 11:54 of the third off Noel Acciari's setup. Joseph Woll stopped 28 of 31, Jet Greaves 17 of 21, and Owen Tippett and Dante Fabbro fought in the second. Columbus played without Sean Monahan and is 7-11-0. Blowing a two-goal lead to the Flyers' offense is like getting outrun by a Zamboni.

Puckline's Report

St. Louis honored Keith Tkachuk before the game, and his sons said thanks by beating the Blues: Brady Tkachuk scored the power-play opener, with Matthew Tkachuk on the assist, in a 4-1 Florida win. Dmitry Kulikov scored his first of the season a minute later, Anton Lundell made it 3-0 in the second, and Sam Reinhart's unassisted goal in the third, his 12th, came on a night he reached 700 career points. Jacob Markstrom stopped 23 of 24 and lost the shutout to Dylan Holloway's power-play goal with 2:06 left. Joel Hofer made 24 saves on 28 in his fourth straight start. Radko Gudas played his 900th game. It was a lovely ceremony for the Tkachuk family, and then the family took two points home to Florida, the most Blues thing imaginable.

Puckline's Report

Jamie Benn got his 1,000th career point, every one of them in a Dallas sweater, and it was the goal that beat Buffalo 2-0. Benn scored at 16:23 of the second off Justin Hryckowian and Nils Lundkvist, and Wyatt Johnston added a power-play goal with 42 seconds left. Jake Oettinger needed only 22 saves for his fourth shutout, which says a lot about the Sabres' night. Alex Lyon was good in his second straight start, 28 saves on 30, and got nothing for it. Dallas is 11-6-2; Buffalo is 8-8-4 and has now been shut out by a goalie who could have played the third period in a recliner. A thousand points for Benn, zero for the Sabres: that's been the Buffalo experience for about 15 years.

Puckline's Report

Ten goals in 65 minutes, two fights and a shootout, and San Jose came out of Utah with a 6-5 win and Utah with a fifth straight loss. Zac Jones scored twice as Utah led 3-1 and 4-3, but the Sharks kept coming: Tyler Toffoli and Adam Gaudette on the power play, Zack Ostapchuk, then Eric Pohlkamp's first NHL goal to tie it at 4 in the third. Dmitry Orlov put the Sharks ahead with 5:43 left and finished with four points; Barrett Hayton tied it again on the power play two minutes later. In the shootout Vincent Trocheck and Macklin Celebrini traded goals before Mason Marchment won it in the fifth round. Karel Vejmelka gave up five on 21 shots (Andre Tourigny said afterward 'Vej has to be better'), and Yaroslav Askarov made 27 saves. Andrew Peeke fought Ty Dellandrea and then Gaudette. Utah's defense went the full 65 minutes without showing up, a real commitment to the bit.

Puckline's Report

Simon Holmstrom picked a good night for his first career hat trick: the Islanders beat Anaheim 6-2, and Mathew Barzal got an assist on Ben Hutton's goal 1:55 into his season debut. Bo Horvat scored on the power play, Holmstrom scored twice in 5:27 of the second, Mitchell Chaffee made it 5-1, and Holmstrom finished the job early in the third. Matthew Schaefer had three assists, because apparently the 19-year-old is also the Isles' playmaker now. Semyon Varlamov stopped 26 of 28; Lukas Dostal stayed in for all 60 minutes and six goals on 25 shots, which is the kind of loyalty usually reserved for a bad contract. Nikita Nesterenko and Cutter Gauthier (his 17th) scored for the Ducks. The Ducks were down 5-1 before the game was half over, then left their goalie out there to absorb a sixth: that's not goaltending support, that's a dare.

Puckline's Report

Calgary opened its road trip with a 3-2 win in Los Angeles, and the Kings helped. Morgan Frost scored early in the second off a Cody Ceci turnover, and Ceci watched the third period from the bench. Joel Armia tied it at 6:21 of the third, Matvei Gridin answered five minutes later for the winner, and Yegor Sharangovich hit the empty net with 1:14 left. Mats Zuccarello's first of the season with the goalie pulled made it close 18 seconds later. Dustin Wolf stopped 29 of 31; Anton Forsberg 21 of 23. The Kings are 5-11-2, level with Chicago at 12 points and ahead of only Vancouver, a Hollywood ending nobody in LA wanted to see.

Puckline Preview

Four days after Edmonton beat the Flyers 3-2 in overtime, the rematch moves to Philadelphia, and both teams are on the second night of a back-to-back. In the last meeting Zach Hyman scored twice in the second, Philadelphia came back on Tyson Foerster's power-play goal and Travis Sanheim's tying goal, and Evan Bouchard ended it 47 seconds into overtime. Bouchard also scored the only goal in Toronto last night, set up by Connor McDavid, who now has a point in all 21 of Edmonton's games and 50 points. Devon Levi got his first NHL shutout in that one, so Tristan Jarry is the likely starter tonight.

The Flyers are 6-10-6, but they just won in Columbus on two goals from Denver Barkey, after spotting the Blue Jackets a 2-0 lead in the first 4:19, a hole they dig so often they should charge rent. Matvei Michkov has 11 goals, while Friedman says Philadelphia wants to make it work with him, and the trade talk around Rasmus Ristolainen won't go away. Joseph Woll played last night, so Dan Vladar is projected. Edmonton is 15-3-3; Philadelphia scores like every goal costs extra.

FLA @ DAL · 8:00 PM ET

Florida PanthersFLA12-7-2 · 26 PTSML +112
@8:00 PM ETSun Nov 15 · American Airlines Center
FLA +112MLDAL -134
Dallas StarsDAL11-6-2 · 24 PTSML -134

Puckline Preview

Florida and Dallas meet for the first time this season, and both played last night, so expect backups: Akira Schmid for the Panthers and Casey DeSmith for the Stars are projected after Jacob Markstrom and Jake Oettinger started Saturday. Dallas comes in feeling good. Jamie Benn got his 1,000th career point, all of them as a Star, in a 2-0 win over Buffalo, and Oettinger needed just 22 saves for his fourth shutout. Mikko Rantanen leads the team with 22 points. The bad news is on the blue line: NHL.com called Miro Heiskanen doubtful for tonight, Lian Bichsel is on IR for a couple of weeks, and Kyle Burroughs was called up from Texas and played Saturday.

The Panthers won 4-1 in St. Louis on the night the Blues honored Keith Tkachuk, with Brady Tkachuk scoring and Matthew setting it up, because nothing says thanks for the ceremony like ruining it. Sam Reinhart reached 700 career points there, and Matthew Tkachuk has 29 points, 25 of them assists. Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand are skating again but are still on the injured list. Florida is 12-7-2, Dallas 11-6-2, and two tired teams with backup goalies is how a Sunday night gets weird.

CGY +126MLANA -152
Anaheim DucksANA10-9-1 · 21 PTSML -152

Puckline Preview

Fourth meeting already, and Anaheim has won two of the first three, including a 5-3 win in Calgary on Nov. 6 when the Ducks scored three in the third and Cutter Gauthier broke the tie with 1:34 left. Gauthier has 17 goals now, and Leo Carlsson leads the team with 27 points, 21 of them assists. Both teams are on back-to-backs. The Ducks got thumped 6-2 by the Islanders last night, Lukas Dostal giving up six on 25 shots, and with Laurent Brossoit sent back to the AHL, the backup plan is less obvious than usual.

Calgary opened its road trip with a 3-2 win in Los Angeles on Matvei Gridin's late goal and 29 saves from Dustin Wolf, so Devin Cooley is the projected starter tonight. Joel Farabee leads the Flames with 18 points, which tells you most of what you need to know about the Flames' offense. Kevin Bahl is out for the season and Jonathan Huberdeau didn't make the trip. Calgary is 9-10-1, Anaheim 10-9-1: two Pacific teams fighting to stay in the race, and one of them is going home from a Sunday night in Anaheim worse off.

VAN @ VGK · 9:00 PM ET

Vancouver CanucksVAN3-17-1 · 7 PTSML +320
@9:00 PM ETSun Nov 15 · T-Mobile Arena
VAN +320MLVGK -420
Vegas Golden KnightsVGK13-5-3 · 29 PTSML -420

Puckline Preview

Vancouver is 3-17-1, has lost seven straight, and gets to snap out of it against a team that has owned it: Vegas beat the Canucks 3-2 at Rogers Arena on Oct. 4 on Marc Gatcomb's go-ahead goal, the Golden Knights' eighth straight win over Vancouver going back to April 2024. The Canucks' last game was a 5-1 loss to the Rangers on Friday, in which the Rangers' Gawdin scored his first two NHL goals, a nice night for him and a long one for the Canucks. Filip Chytil is back, Cameron Crotty made his Canucks debut on defense, and Leevi Meriläinen is projected in goal again with Thatcher Demko still out. Elias Pettersson leads the team with 21 points.

Vegas is 13-5-3 and coming off a shootout loss to Nashville on Friday, when Juuse Saros stopped 40. Jack Eichel has 26 points and Mitch Marner 21 assists, and Noah Hanifin is out week to week. Adin Hill and Carter Hart have alternated the last five starts, so Hart may get this one. The Canucks have seven points all season, which in Las Vegas terms is a gambler who stopped counting a long time ago.

NSH @ SJS · 9:00 PM ET

Nashville PredatorsNSH11-4-5 · 27 PTSML -164
@9:00 PM ETSun Nov 15 · SAP Center at San Jose
NSH -164MLSJS +136
San Jose SharksSJS9-11-2 · 20 PTSML +136

Puckline Preview

Nashville arrives in San Jose on a seven-game winning streak, the last a shootout win in Vegas on Friday when Ryan O'Reilly scored twice and Juuse Saros stopped 40 shots. Saros is projected again on two days' rest, and he came into this season 15-2-1 against the Sharks with a .925 save percentage. The Sharks did beat him once already, though: 3-2 in a shootout in Nashville on Oct. 15. Steven Stamkos has 11 goals and Roman Josi 21 assists, and Jonathan Marchessault is day to day; tonight was one of his reported return targets, but nothing is confirmed.

The Sharks won a 6-5 shootout in Utah last night: Eric Pohlkamp scored his first NHL goal, Dmitry Orlov had four points and Mason Marchment won it in the fifth round. That was Yaroslav Askarov's start, so Alex Nedeljkovic is projected tonight, which means Nashville doesn't get the Askarov reunion; the Predators traded him to San Jose in 2024. Macklin Celebrini leads San Jose with 24 points; Alexander Wennberg sat out Saturday and is day to day. The Sharks are 9-11-2 and just gave up five goals to a Utah team that had lost four straight, which a Nashville team that has won seven straight will have noticed.

By Puckline Prince
